---
title: Keep a copy in sync
description: Follow an instance's event stream from a cursor, so a copy of your data stays current and picks up where it stopped after a break.
---

A search index, a cache or a report keeps its own copy of an instance's data. Read it once, then apply each change from the [event stream](/build/events) and save a cursor, so after a break you receive everything you missed and nothing twice. The [Swift SDK](/reference/swift-sdk) does this for you ([Devices](/build/working-copies)).

You need your own Marfa instance, with the CLI signed in to it, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you. This guide keeps a copy of files, so make a key that reads `core.file` and its subtypes:

```bash
marfa keys create --label "File copy" --source file-copy --type-permission "core.file.*=read"
```

Set `MARFA_API_URL` to your instance's address, such as `http://localhost:8600`, and `MARFA_API_KEY` to the key.

## What the stream sends

From cursor `21`, narrowed to files, `marfa events` prints one frame a line:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa events --type core.file --edges none --cursor 21
```

```text
-  stream_cursor  25
22  item.created  01a1f126-5ad1-7029-8f69-a66a15ee406d
23  item.trashed  01a1f124-12c1-7762-af28-52450dd463af
24  item.updated  01a1f126-5ad1-7029-8f69-a66a15ee406d
25  item.purged  01a1f124-12c1-7762-af28-52450dd463af
-  stream_live  25
```

</Terminal>

Over HTTP, the [stream](/reference/api/event-stream/streamEvents) takes your cursor in the `Last-Event-ID` header and answers server-sent events. Here it is from cursor `24`, with the item cut short:

```http title="Request"
GET /events?type=core.file&edges=none
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Last-Event-ID: 24
```

```sse title="Response" status="200" note="Server-sent events"
event: stream_cursor
data: {"event_type":"stream_cursor","cursor":"25"}

id: 25
event: item.purged
data: {"event_type":"item.purged","item":{"id":"01a1f124-12c1-7762-af28-52450dd463af","type":"core.file","state":"trashed",...},"metadata":{...}}

event: stream_live
data: {"event_type":"stream_live","cursor":"25"}
```

The stream opens with `stream_cursor`, which names the **head of the log**, the latest event, then replays every event after your cursor, sends `stream_live` once caught up, and sends each new event. Only events carry an `id:` line, so **the last `id:` you received is always a cursor you can resume from**. While the stream is quiet, Marfa sends a `:ping` comment every 30 seconds.

## Build the sync

`sync.ts` keeps a copy of every file item in a JSON file.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Read the frames

A browser `EventSource` can't send an `Authorization` header, and the [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) doesn't read streams, so read the stream with `fetch`:

```ts title="sync.ts"
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createClient, pages, type components } from "@withmarfa/client";

const baseUrl = process.env.MARFA_API_URL!;
const credential = process.env.MARFA_API_KEY!;
const marfa = createClient({ baseUrl, credential });

type Frame = { id?: string; event: string; data: string };

async function* readFrames(body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>>): AsyncGenerator<Frame> {
  let buffer = "";
  for await (const text of body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream())) {
    buffer += text;
    const blocks = buffer.split("\n\n");
    buffer = blocks.pop() ?? "";
    for (const block of blocks) {
      const frame: Frame = { event: "message", data: "" };
      for (const line of block.split("\n")) {
        if (line.startsWith(":")) continue; // a comment, such as the ping
        const colon = line.indexOf(":");
        const field = colon === -1 ? line : line.slice(0, colon);
        const value = colon === -1 ? "" : line.slice(colon + 1).replace(/^ /, "");
        if (field === "id") frame.id = value;
        else if (field === "event") frame.event = value;
        else if (field === "data") frame.data += (frame.data ? "\n" : "") + value;
      }
      if (frame.data !== "") yield frame;
    }
  }
}

async function open(cursor?: string): Promise<ReadableStream<Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>>> {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/events?type=core.file&edges=none`, {
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${credential}`,
      ...(cursor === undefined ? {} : { "Last-Event-ID": cursor }),
    },
  });
  if (!response.ok || response.body === null) {
    throw new Error(`The stream answered ${response.status}`);
  }
  return response.body;
}
```

Take each frame as it arrives: Marfa closes a reader that takes nothing for 30 seconds while a frame waits.

</Step>
<Step>

### Keep the copy and its cursor together

Save the cursor **in the same place as the copy, in step with what you apply**: here, one file written after each event. An item event carries the item as it stands after the change, so `apply` replaces what the copy holds, or removes it for `item.purged`; `item.trashed` keeps it, in the bin. `metadata.changed` carries the item too.

```ts title="sync.ts"
type Item = components["schemas"]["Item"];
type Copy = { cursor?: string; files: Record<string, Item> };
const file = "files-copy.json";
let copy: Copy = await readFile(file, "utf8").then(JSON.parse, () => ({ files: {} }));

function apply(event: { event_type: string; item: Item }) {
  if (event.event_type === "item.purged") delete copy.files[event.item.id];
  else if (event.event_type.startsWith("item.") || event.event_type === "metadata.changed") {
    copy.files[event.item.id] = event.item;
  }
}

async function saveCursor(cursor: string) {
  copy.cursor = cursor;
  await writeFile(file, JSON.stringify(copy));
}
```

`apply` passes over `rows.changed`, which names its item only by `id`, `type` and `source` ([Tables](/build/tables)).

</Step>
<Step>

### Follow the stream

`follow` applies each event, saves its ID, and returns the frame that ended the stream, or `closed`:

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function follow(cursor: string): Promise<string> {
  for await (const frame of readFrames(await open(cursor))) {
    const data = JSON.parse(frame.data);
    switch (frame.event) {
      case "stream_cursor":
        break;
      case "stream_live":
        await saveCursor(data.cursor);
        break;
      case "stream_incomplete":
      case "catchup_too_old":
      case "cursor_ahead":
        return frame.event;
      default:
        apply(data);
        await saveCursor(frame.id!);
    }
  }
  return "closed";
}
```

It saves the `cursor` of `stream_live` too, because on a narrow stream the last event can be far behind the head. Marfa sends each event after your cursor exactly once, even across a server restart.

</Step>
<Step>

### Start from the head of the log

`rebuild` takes the head from the first frame, lists every file in every state, then saves the head as the cursor, so every change made while it lists waits in the log. The listing and the stream ask for the same items, so the copy holds exactly what the stream keeps current.

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function rebuild(): Promise<string> {
  let head: string | undefined;
  for await (const frame of readFrames(await open())) {
    if (frame.event === "stream_cursor") head = JSON.parse(frame.data).cursor;
    break; // closes the stream
  }
  if (head === undefined) throw new Error("The stream didn't name the head of the log");
  copy = { files: {} };
  const files = pages(async (cursor) => {
    const { data, error } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
      params: { query: { type: "core.file", state: "any", cursor } },
    });
    if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
    return data;
  });
  for await (const item of files) apply({ event_type: "item.created", item: item as Item });
  await saveCursor(head);
  return head;
}
```

When Marfa can't read the head, the first frame is `stream_incomplete` with the reason `read_failed`, and `rebuild` throws.

</Step>
<Step>

### Run it

The loop resumes from the saved cursor after a break, and rebuilds when the cursor can't be used:

```ts title="sync.ts"
let cursor = copy.cursor; // undefined on the first run
for (;;) {
  cursor ??= await rebuild();
  const ended = await follow(cursor);
  cursor = ended === "catchup_too_old" || ended === "cursor_ahead" ? undefined : copy.cursor;
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
}
```

Run it as an ES module. Add a file with `marfa items add`, move it to the bin, and `files-copy.json` follows each change.

</Step>
</Steps>

## When the stream ends

| You see | It means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The connection closes with no frame | A network fault, or your reader took nothing for 30 seconds. | Wait a moment, then resume from your saved cursor. |
| `stream_incomplete` | The stream couldn't go on, for its `reason`: `server_stopping`, `read_failed` or `credential_ended`. | Resume from your saved cursor; for `credential_ended`, with a valid key. |
| `catchup_too_old` | The log no longer holds the events after your cursor. It keeps them 30 days by default (`event_log_retention_days`). | Rebuild from the head of the log. |
| `cursor_ahead` | Your cursor is past the log's head, as after a restore from a backup. | Discard the cursor and rebuild from the head of the log. |

`marfa events` exits `1` for `cursor_ahead` and `catchup_too_old`, `3` for a `stream_incomplete` a new stream can mend, and `5` for `credential_ended` ([Exit codes](/reference/cli#exit-codes)).

If the stream is refused before it opens, `open` throws. After `429 rate_limited`, wait the seconds `Retry-After` names. After `503 stream_capacity_exhausted`, the instance is serving all the streams it allows: try again later. Any other refusal, such as `403 type_not_permitted` or `400 validation_error` for a cursor the log didn't write, is a fault in the key or the request to fix, not retry. [Stream change events](/reference/api/event-stream/streamEvents) lists every answer.

## Narrow the stream

`type` takes up to ten types or patterns, such as `app.*`, each with its subtypes: repeat `--type` in the CLI, or separate them with commas over HTTP. Edge events come whatever `type` says, so `sync.ts` sends `edges=none`. A stream that names a `type` never carries `attention.raised`.

A cursor works under any filter, so you can change filters between connections.

The rules behind this guide are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) chapter of the contract.
